Marathon Petroleum stock bounced back 3.1% today after a brutal five-day slide that erased 13% of its value. The timing and scale of the recovery align with today's news that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio signaled stalled Iran negotiations—a geopolitical de-escalation signal that typically removes uncertainty about potential oil supply disruptions and can ease pressure on energy stocks that had been sold off on war-risk premiums.

The deeper context: the stock has been hammered since early November, likely triggered by the midterm election outcome shifting Congress toward Democratic control, which the market read as potential headwinds for refining (through stricter environmental policy and offshore drilling limits). Today's rebound, modest as it is, suggests some traders are selectively re-entering positions now that Mideast tension has cooled, even though broader refining margins remain under pressure—U.S. oil is at $99.64 per barrel while refineries are running at 94.5% capacity with above-average gasoline and diesel inventories, both factors that typically constrain profit.
